title: Does the trapezium strip have angles of symmetry?
description: A strip shaped like a trapezium has a dot at its centre. A half turn puts the longer side on top, so the strip does not overlap itself, and only the full turn works. Keeko's doubt is that it looks balanced, so it fits after a half turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shape with a shorter top side and a longer bottom side cannot overlap itself after a half turn, so only the full turn works and it has no rotational symmetry. Watch for students who trust how balanced a shape looks.

source: Find the angles of symmetry of the following strip. The stri
video_script.why: The child turns a strip with a shorter top side by a half turn, sees that the longer side lands on top, and finds that only the full turn brings it back.
video_script.substitution: Turn the strip by a half turn about its dot and compare the top and bottom sides with the start picture.
video_script.anchor: a strip shaped like a trapezium, shorter on top and longer at the bottom, with equal slanting sides and a dot at its centre
video_script.wrong_answer: it looks balanced, so it fits after a half turn
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says it looks balanced, so it fits after a half turn. After the half turn the longer side is on top, but in the start picture the shorter side is on top, so the turned strip does not fit.
video_script.payoff_line: Only the full turn of three hundred and sixty degrees works

final_answer.value: Only 360 degrees; the strip has no rotational symmetry
final_answer.spoken: only the full turn of three hundred and sixty degrees works

maths_rules: A turn about the centre after which a shape looks exactly the same is called an angle of symmetry
A shape that matches itself after a turn smaller than the full turn has rotational symmetry
A half turn of 180 degrees puts the longer side of the strip on top, where the start picture has the shorter side, so the strip does not overlap itself
A quarter turn and a three quarter turn stand the flat sides upright, but the strip has no upright sides, so they do not fit either
Two half turns make 360 degrees, which brings the strip back, so only the full turn works
The strip has no rotational symmetry
video_script.design: One idea: the strip has a shorter top side and a longer bottom side, so no turn smaller than the full turn fits. The strip stays on the board all video. Wrong idea: it looks balanced, so it fits after a half turn.
